Dear Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and Members of the Committee,
Thank you for the time your committee recently took to review LD1196, a Resolve to Require the Towns of Kittery and York to Develop a Boundary Description.
I understand there were questions at the recent hearing on the proposed legislation, including whether the proposed resolve is supported by both the Town of Kittery and the Town of York. I am happy to report to you that the proposed resolution is in fact supported by both towns.
In late fall of 2024, the Kittery Town Council and York Selectboard decided to work together to resolve concerns that the currently acknowledged boundary line between the two towns may differ from another historical boundary line established by Massachusetts colonial authorities. When the two towns decided to work together to resolve the boundary line question, it was understood that any permanent resolution would likely entail formal action by the Legislature.
Since that time, the two towns have issued a joint Request for Qualifications for shared survey services, and we are working together to select a surveyor to complete a formal description of the currently acknowledged boundary line. We anticipate that such a description will be required before the Legislature can act to formally resolve this issue. Our intent is to provide that description on or before December 3, 2025.
Thank you for your time and consideration of LD1196. If you have any further questions, or if you would like representatives of the Town of Kittery to appear before the Committee to discuss the proposed resolve further, please do not hesitate to contact me at 207-4751329 or at kamaral@kitteryme.org.
Sincerely,

Kendra Amaral Town Manager

Testimony of Senator Mark W. Lawrence introducing
LD 1196, Resolve, to Require the Towns of Kittery and York to Develop a Boundary Description
Before the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government April 2, 2025
Chair Baldacci, Chair Salisbury and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and
Local Government, my name is Mark Lawrence. I am the State Senator from District 35 in southern York County, proudly representing Eliot, Kittery, Ogunquit, South Berwick, and York. I am here to introduce LD 1196, Resolve, to Require the Towns of Kittery and York to Develop a Boundary
Description.
Working with Kittery Town Manager Kendra Amaral and York Town Manager Peter Joseph
respectively, I present this bill after a town line boundary discrepancy between Kittery and York was revealed in a development approval in Kittery a few years back. Action was taken to settle this dispute in York County Superior Court. However, it was dismissed after Judge Douglas stated that an official boundary inspection was required first.
In an effort to settle this neighborly dispute, the towns agreed to jointly petition this body, the Maine Legislature, to reach a compromise and determine the current town borders. This resolve requires the
Town of Kittery and the Town of York to jointly develop a description, in metes and bounds, of the
boundary between the two towns based on the assessing maps in each of the towns.
From there, the towns are required to jointly provide the description to the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government, which may report out a bill to the Second Regular Session of the l32nd Legislature establishing the boundary between the two towns.
In my district, we work together to solve local issues with local solutions. In this case, these towns are
seeking the authorization from the Legislature to do just that. This committee has the opportunity to enable these two historic towns to settle this dispute and provide clarity for their residents, business owners and property tax payers. For those reasons, I respectfully encourage you to support this bill.
Thank you for the opportunity to bring this legislation forward. I am happy to answer any questions you may have or bring additional information to the Committee for the work session.
